A1.justification: Both PDFs describe XTrack and its MeME framework. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support comparison. V1's Appendix S.1–S.2 was inspected; the supplied v2 ends with references and contains no appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original tracking experiments on five benchmarks, component and expert-count ablations, and appendix analyses of routing and tracking attributes.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark results for XTrack-B/L, expanded component ablations, multimodal training and zero-shot transfer experiments, and routing analyses.

M1.justification: V1 presents shallow X embedding and deep prompting of an RGB tracker; v2 Section 3.1/Figure 3 specifies bidirectional RGB/X transformer updates with MeME at attention and FFN stages. V2 also deliberately weakens classifier supervision to enable cross-modal expert use, contrasting with the near-exclusive modality assignment validated in v1 Appendix S.1. Shared experts, edge gating, and low-dimensional prompting remain.

E1.justification: The same five datasets and three auxiliary modalities remain. V2 Table 6 adds a limited but distinct scenario: zero-shot tracking on modalities absent from training, including depth and thermal evaluation after event-only training. V1's cross-dataset evaluations retained training exposure to the tested modality.

E2.justification: V2 substantially expands the evaluated comparators, including OSTrack, OneTracker, and SDSTrack across the benchmark tables, plus additional specialist trackers. OneTracker and SDSTrack were cited but not evaluated in v1. Some comparisons disappear: Stark_d is absent from VOT-RGBD2022, and DAFNet/MaCNet no longer have LasHeR results despite remaining in the RGBT234 comparison.

E3.justification: The reported batch size changes from 64 to 32, training from 60 to 90 epochs, and learning-rate decay from epoch 48 to 78. V2 evaluates OSTrack-based XTrack-B and an additional DropMAE-based XTrack-L. It also introduces training-modality subsets and rigid/soft routing comparisons. These are substantive reported setting changes, not merely additional implementation disclosure.

E4.justification: V2 extends shared/specialized-expert and expert-count ablations from DepthTrack to all three training benchmarks. It adds joint-training and zero-shot analyses, routing-strength comparisons, and three scene-specific routing case studies. V1's appendix-wide event-routing histogram and RGBT234 attribute radar analysis are absent rather than simply relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests for its experimental results. V2 retains point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: V2 replaces the original XTrack results and adds B/L results: DepthTrack F-score is 59.7 in v1 versus 61.5/64.8; LasHeR precision is 65.5 versus 69.1/73.1; VisEvent precision is 75.6 versus 77.5/80.5. These are results under revised training/model settings, not controlled same-setting gains. Ablation results also change, new transfer/routing results appear, and some retained baseline values change, including DDiMP recall from 46.9 to 56.9.

T1.justification: V2 adds mathematical definitions of the coupled attention and FFN residual updates in Equations 1–2, extending v1's formal description of the pipeline. The routing, classification/balance losses, expert fusion, and prompting mathematics are otherwise largely retained with notation changes. Neither version contains theorem or proof contributions.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from a generalist, modality-blind tracker positioned toward AGI to cross-modal knowledge sharing through deliberately weak classification. V2 foregrounds a claimed first systematic transfer approach and an average three-point precision advantage over SOTA, replacing v1's emphasis on competitive specialist-level performance with small tuning overhead.

C2.justification: V1 treats accurate modality assignment as evidence of successful specialization; v2 interprets classification confusion as an opportunity for knowledge transfer. V2 adds explanations of event-to-thermal versus event-to-depth transfer and scene-dependent expert selection. Its limitations emphasize identical expert designs and adaptive computation, while dropping v1's explicit qualifications about known training modalities, specialist inferiority, and data requirements.

D1.justification: V2 explicitly reports top-k = 2, a 0.001 loss proportion, and backbone sources for its two variants. It removes v1's approximate 100M total and 8M additional parameter counts. The availability statement changes from a promised code/model release to stated public source-code availability; that availability was not independently checked.

R1.justification: Research positioning substantially shifts from AGI-oriented unification to knowledge transfer across otherwise isolated modality-specific trackers and experts. V2 replaces much of the broad generalist/NLP context with tracking literature and adds works such as DropMAE and LLaMA-MoE. Its novelty argument now centers on cross-modal sharing rather than principally blind, single-parameter-set tracking.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Related work is reframed, an Overall Pipeline subsection is introduced, and experiments are reorganized from within/out-of-distribution sections into depth, thermal, and event sections. Ablations and discussion become a separate major section, and the appendix structure disappears.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout, redesigns the motivation and pipeline displays, regroups benchmark tables by modality, and adds training/routing tables and scene visualizations. Core expert diagrams are partly retained. V2 also introduces reporting problems: RGBT234 metric headings are reversed relative to retained baseline values, and Figure 2 labels as AUC values matching Table 6's precision results.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens support for cross-modal knowledge sharing: Table 6 directly tests training-modality combinations, Table 7 compares routing alternatives, and component ablations cover all three modalities. These address v1's largely indirect evidence for joint-training benefits, while expanded comparator coverage improves validation. The RGBT234 heading error, Figure 2 metric mismatch, and removal of parameter-count and attribute details weaken reporting, but the direct empirical tests provide a substantial net improvement.
